sections.title: Overview
descriptions: This page brings together available records related to Joseph Ferreri’s encounter with the American Fork Police Department.

sections.title: Criminal Cases
descriptions: The criminal-case records associated with this encounter are organized below.

contents.text_value: Joseph Ferreri was charged in Utah with aggravated exploitation of prostitution, engaging in a pattern of unlawful activity, human trafficking, and money laundering. All four charges were dismissed without prejudice on December 8, 2021.

Wang Ju Ying, Ferreri’s wife, was separately charged in Utah with two misdemeanor prostitution counts and one felony count of engaging in a pattern of unlawful activity. All three charges were dismissed without prejudice on January 28, 2022.

Wang had previously been charged in Bryan County, Oklahoma, in March 2017 with offering to engage in prostitution after an arrest at the Red Lotus Spa in Calera, where she worked. Wang and Ferreri had married in Texas the previous month. In November 2017, the Oklahoma court dismissed the case without costs because Wang was being held at the Tulsa County Detention Center on an immigration detainer. The dismissal record does not state that she was deported or that deportation was certain. A later federal complaint states that the Department of Homeland Security issued Wang a visa recognizing her as Ferreri’s spouse on May 14, 2018.

sections.title: Media Coverage
descriptions: News coverage is grouped according to whether it reported the initial arrests or the later challenge to Ferreri’s arrest and prosecution.

contents.text_value: Initial news coverage focused on the massage-parlor investigation and law-enforcement allegations involving prostitution and human trafficking.
Later reporting focused on the dropped prostitution charges, Ferreri’s account of the consequences of the allegations, and his civil lawsuit against the police.
